About me

Hello, I'm the Creator of Sanskriti

A little about me

I'm Agastya, an MYP 4 student. I built Sanskriti for my Digital Design project, as part of Service as Action.

My interests:

DesignIndian cultureMusicTechnology

Why this issue matters to me

Traditional Indian skills carry stories, knowledge and identity. I noticed that young people like me rarely get to see these skills, or know where to try them. I wanted to make a place that makes discovering them easy and fun.

What creating this website taught me

  1. 01

    Research skills

    Finding reliable sources and checking facts before I use them.

  2. 02

    Design skills

    Colour, type, layout, and how to make pages easy to read.

  3. 03

    Designing for an audience

    Making every choice with 8–18 year olds in mind.

  4. 04

    The bigger picture

    How design and technology can help keep culture alive.

My design process

  1. 1. Research

    Studied the problem and analysed existing websites.

  2. 2. Wireframes

    Sketched the layout of every page.

  3. 3. Design options

    Tried colour palettes and styles, then got feedback.

  4. 4. Final website

    Built, tested and published Sanskriti.

My hope for Sanskriti

I hope Sanskriti helps at least one young person find a tradition they love, and then go and try it for real, with the people who keep it alive.

– Agastya

Privacy & safety

  • Sanskriti has no accounts, no analytics, no cookies and no tracking. It never sends your information anywhere.
  • Your browser saves a few things on this device only: your quiz result, your streak (a date and a number), the skills you viewed recently, and your pledge ticks.
  • The live map on Find Experiences only loads from Google Maps if you press "Show map".
  • Links to other websites open in a new tab. Ask a parent, guardian or teacher if you're unsure.
  • Always visit workshops and places with a trusted adult.
